subject: geography
title: TNC Strategies & Production
welcome_lead: Map Coca-Cola, Nike and Tesla global networks.
meta_desc: A-Level Geography adventure on TNC strategies, production networks and Nike case study.
final_note: TNCs orchestrate dispersed production at global scale.

concepts.def: Transnational corporation with operations in 2+ countries; UNCTAD lists 80000+.
Control multiple production stages; Apple controls chip design, design, retail.
Contracting to external firms; Nike has no factories of its own.
Factory with poor conditions; Nike supply chain controversies 1990s.
Adapting products to local tastes; Coke uses different sugar levels per market.

walkthroughs.body_html: Sold in 200 countries; 1.9 billion servings/day. Concentrate produced centrally; bottlers operate franchises locally. Indian Plachimada plant closed 2005 over groundwater extraction; Mexican obesity rate (74 percent overweight) partly linked to per capita 728 8oz servings/yr.

Nike outsources 100 percent of production; 500+ factories employ 1 million workers across 41 countries. Vietnam alone produces 50 percent. 1990s sweatshop scandals (child labour, $1.60/hr wages) forced FairLabor reforms. CEO pay-worker ratio remains controversial.

Tesla controls battery cells (Gigafactory Nevada), motor design, software, supercharger network, retail. Different from outsource-heavy auto industry. Shanghai Gigafactory (2019) produces 50 percent of global Teslas. Demonstrates revival of vertical integration in high-tech.
